source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AC-2 Account Management (public control family summary for eval)
text: Organizations shall manage system accounts, including establishing, activating, modifying, disabling, and removing accounts. Account managers shall authorize access based on a valid access authorization and intended system usage. Privileged account creation shall require prior approval from authorized personnel under least privilege.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AC-3 Access Enforcement
text: The information system shall enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies. Access enforcement shall implement least privilege and shall deny access by default when authorization is missing.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AC-6 Least Privilege
text: Organizations shall employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users and processes that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks. Elevation of privileges shall require explicit authorization and shall be audited.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — IA-2 Identification and Authentication
text: The information system shall uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users. Privileged accounts shall use multi-factor authentication. Machine identities used by automation shall be authenticated before tool invocation or remote execution.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — IA-5 Authenticator Management
text: Organizations shall manage authenticators and shall protect credentials and cryptographic keys from unauthorized disclosure. Systems shall not expose secret material in logs. Access tokens shall be stored with confidentiality protections.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — SI-3 Malicious Code Protection
text: Organizations shall implement malicious code protection. Automated agents shall not execute untrusted code from external sources without sandbox controls. Untrusted input shall not be passed to system command interpreters without validation and prior authorization.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — SI-4 System Monitoring
text: Organizations shall monitor the information system to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks. Security-relevant events from automation and service accounts shall be logged. Audit read access for monitoring tools shall follow least privilege.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AU-2 Event Logging
text: Organizations shall determine that the information system must audit specific events. Privileged access, network egress from production, and configuration changes shall generate audit records. Audit logs shall be protected from unauthorized modification.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — CM-3 Configuration Change Control
text: Organizations shall determine and document types of changes that require prior approval. Configuration changes to production systems shall require management approval before deployment. Automated pipelines shall not apply unreviewed destructive changes.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — CM-5 Access Restrictions for Change
text: Organizations shall define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to the information system. Only authorized personnel with explicit authorization may modify production baselines.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — SC-7 Boundary Protection
text: Organizations shall monitor and control communications at external boundaries. Network egress of sensitive data shall require authorization. Automated agents shall not open unrestricted outbound connections from production without policy approval.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — SC-8 Transmission Confidentiality
text: The information system shall protect the confidentiality of transmitted information. Credentials and access tokens shall not be transmitted in cleartext. Secret material in transit shall use approved encryption.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — SC-28 Protection of Information at Rest
text: The information system shall protect the confidentiality of information at rest. Cryptographic keys and stored credentials shall be protected. Systems shall not store secret material in world-readable locations.

source_title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — MP-6 Media Sanitization
text: Organizations shall sanitize digital media prior to disposal or reuse. Destructive wiping of storage that may contain credentials shall require prior authorization and shall be audited as a privileged operation.

source_title: CISA — Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks (public guidance summary)
text: Organizations must train personnel not to execute untrusted attachments or links. Automation shall not process untrusted email content as system commands. Suspicious content shall be analyzed in a sandbox, not on production hosts.

source_title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog — operational expectation summary
text: Federal civilian executive branch agencies must remediate vulnerabilities in the KEV catalog by due dates. Privileged access used for emergency patching shall be authorized and audited. Unauthenticated network exposure of known-exploited services shall not remain without compensating controls.

source_title: NIST SP 800-63B Digital Identity Guidelines — Authenticator assurance summary
text: Authenticators shall be protected against unauthorized capture. Verifiers shall not store secrets as plaintext passwords. Session tokens shall be protected and shall not be logged. Automated processes using authenticators shall follow least privilege.

source_title: NIST SP 800-218 SSDF — secure software development practice summary
text: Organizations shall protect all forms of code from unauthorized access and tampering. Changes to production software shall require review and authorization. Automated agents committing to mainline branches shall operate under least privilege and audited identities.

source_title: OMB M-22-09 Federal Zero Trust Strategy — public policy summary for eval
text: Agencies shall implement zero trust architecture principles including explicit authorization before access. Network location alone shall not imply trust. Privileged access and automation identities shall authenticate and be authorized continuously where feasible.

source_title: NIST AI RMF 1.0 — Govern function summary for automation
text: Organizations shall establish policies for AI system risk management. High-impact automated actions that can modify systems or exfiltrate data shall require human oversight and prior authorization. Accountability for automated agent actions shall be assigned.
